record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: For the generalized Lamé differential equation, give a modern proof of Heine’s claim about the number of Van Vleck polynomials that produce polynomial solutions, and characterize the exceptional cases in which the number of distinct Van Vleck polynomials is strictly smaller than the generic Heine count.

evidence.quote: As far as I know, there is no modern proof of Heine’s result. Also, is it possible to characterize the exceptional cases when the number of different Van Vleck polynomials is strictly less than ... ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the generalized Lamé differential equation
$$A(z)\,p''(z) + 2B(z)\,p'(z) + C(z)\,p(z) = 0,$$
where $A(z)=\prod_{j=1}^{N}(z-a_j)$ with pairwise distinct complex numbers $a_1,\dots,a_N$, and $B(z)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $N-1$ written as
$$\frac{B(z)}{A(z)} = \sum_{j=1}^{N} \frac{\rho_j}{z-a_j}, \qquad \rho_j\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}.$$
For a given integer $n\ge 0$, a Van Vleck polynomial is a polynomial $C(z)$ of degree at most $N-2$ such that the equation above admits a (Heine–Stieltjes) polynomial solution $p(z)$ of degree exactly $n$. Heine claimed that, in the generic case, the number of distinct Van Vleck polynomials producing a polynomial solution of degree $n$ equals
$$\sigma(n,N) := \binom{n+N-2}{n}.$$

(a) Provide a complete modern proof of Heine's count: under suitable genericity assumptions on the parameters $(a_j,\rho_j)$, the number of distinct Van Vleck polynomials $C(z)$ for which the generalized Lamé equation has a polynomial solution of degree exactly $n$ is exactly $\sigma(n,N)$.

(b) Characterize all exceptional configurations of the parameters $(a_1,\dots,a_N;\rho_1,\dots,\rho_N)$ for which the number of distinct Van Vleck polynomials producing a degree-$n$ polynomial solution is strictly less than $\sigma(n,N)$.
artifact.status_search_result: There has been substantial modern work on Heine–Stieltjes and Van Vleck polynomials (asymptotics, interlacing, zero distribution, complex parameter regimes, BCS/Bethe ansatz connections), and several authors have given modern arguments establishing Heine's generic count in particular settings. However, a complete characterization of all exceptional parameter configurations giving a strictly smaller number of distinct Van Vleck polynomials does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature, so the status is best classified as unknown / partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: On the zeros of complex Van Vleck polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: strengthening Heine's classical result on the number of possible Van Vleck polynomials in the complex case with three free parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Modern partial results on Heine's count exist but are limited in scope.

status_evidence.title: Interlacing and non-orthogonality of spectral polynomials for the Lamé operator
status_evidence.snippet: Interlacing properties of Stieltjes/Van Vleck polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature addresses related structural properties but not full exceptional characterization.
